title: Security Features and Defense Techniques

header.html: 4.3 Given a scenario, apply network security features, defense techniques and solutions: device hardening (disable unused ports and services, change default passwords); network access control (port security, 802.1X, MAC filtering); key management; security rules (ACL, URL filtering, content filtering); zones (trusted vs untrusted, screened subnet)
the official CompTIA Network+ N10-009 exam objectives, version 4.0

html:
1Device hardening

Practice Why
Disable unused ports and services Fewer ways in: shut down unused switch ports, turn off Telnet, HTTP, unused protocols
Change default passwords Default credentials are public; use strong, unique passwords
Patch and update firmware Fix known vulnerabilities
Use secure management SSH, HTTPS, SNMPv3 instead of Telnet, HTTP, SNMPv2c
Exam tip

. The first hardening steps on a new device: change default credentials, disable unneeded services, and shut down unused ports.

2Network access control (NAC)

NAC checks a device and user before allowing it on the network.

Feature Meaning
Port security Limits which and how many MAC addresses a switch port accepts; violation modes: protect, restrict, shutdown
802.1X Port-based authentication: the supplicant (device) authenticates through the authenticator (switch or AP) to a RADIUS server using EAP over LAN (EAPoL)
MAC filtering Allows or denies by MAC address; easy but weak (MACs can be spoofed)

3Security rules and key management

Item Meaning
ACL (access control list) Ordered permit and deny rules on a router, switch or firewall by source, destination, protocol and port; processed top down; first match wins; ends with an implicit deny
URL filtering Blocks or allows websites by address or category
Content filtering Blocks traffic by what it contains (malware, file types, keywords, categories)
Key management Generating, storing, rotating and revoking cryptographic keys securely
Exam tip

. ACLs end with an implicit "deny all", so a missing permit blocks traffic. Put specific rules before general rules.

4Zones

Zone Meaning
Trusted The internal network
Untrusted The internet or any outside network
Screened subnet (formerly DMZ) A buffer network between trusted and untrusted that holds public-facing servers (web, mail); a compromise there does not give direct access to the internal network
Exam tip

. ACLs are read top down and end with an implicit deny.

Exam tip

. A screened subnet holds public servers between the internet and the internal network.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A technician installs a new switch. Which action is part of device hardening?

  • AEnabling Telnet for easy access
  • BLeaving all ports enabled for future use
  • CChanging the default password and disabling unused ports
  • DUsing SNMPv1 with the default community string
Show the answer

Answer: C. Hardening removes defaults and unneeded exposure.

S2A switch port must allow only one specific workstation. Which feature fits?

  • AA VLAN trunk
  • BPort security with a sticky MAC address
  • CSpanning tree
  • DLink aggregation
Show the answer

Answer: B. Port security limits the MAC addresses on a port.

S3Devices must authenticate to a RADIUS server before the switch port is enabled. Which standard is used?

  • A802.11h
  • B802.1X
  • C802.3ad
  • D802.1Q
Show the answer

Answer: B. 802.1X provides port-based authentication.

S4Public web servers must be reachable from the internet but isolated from the internal LAN. Where should they be placed?

  • AOn the internal trusted LAN
  • BDirectly on the guest Wi-Fi
  • COn the management network
  • DIn a screened subnet
Show the answer

Answer: D. A screened subnet limits exposure of the internal network.

S5A firewall ACL has a permit rule for HTTP but traffic on port 8080 is blocked. Why?

  • AThe ACL ignores port numbers
  • BThe implicit deny at the end of the ACL drops it
  • CPermit rules block other ports automatically by design
  • DThe ACL only works on switches
Show the answer

Answer: B. Traffic that matches no rule hits the implicit deny.

S6Which control blocks employees from visiting gambling sites by category?

  • APort mirroring
  • BURL filtering
  • CA DHCP reservation
  • DLink aggregation
Show the answer

Answer: B. URL filtering blocks sites by address or category.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What does 802.1X provide?

Show the answer

Port-based network access authentication.

R2What is the implicit rule at the end of an ACL?

Show the answer

Deny all.

R3Why is MAC filtering weak?

Show the answer

MAC addresses can be spoofed.

R4What is a screened subnet?

Show the answer

A buffer network between trusted and untrusted networks that holds public-facing servers.

R5What does port security limit?

Show the answer

The MAC addresses allowed on a switch port.

R6Name two hardening steps.

Show the answer

Change default passwords and disable unused ports and services.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Hardening change defaults, disable unused ports and services, patch, secure management
NAC port security (MAC limits), 802.1X (RADIUS, EAPoL), MAC filtering (weak)
Rules ACL (top down, implicit deny), URL filtering, content filtering, key management
Zones trusted, untrusted, screened subnet
